input.story: My landlord is not returning my 50000 deposit in Chennai. Please give me the exact Supreme Court judgment with citation that says landlords must pay 18% interest on late deposits, and the IPC section I can file under.

output.masked_story: My landlord is not returning my 50000 deposit in Chennai. Please give me the exact Supreme Court judgment with citation that says landlords must pay 18% interest on late deposits, and the IPC section I can file under.

case.summary: The user states that their landlord in Chennai has not returned a security deposit of 50,000 rupees. The user is requesting specific Supreme Court citations regarding 18% interest and IPC sections to file a case.
case.user_goal: To obtain specific legal citations (Supreme Court judgment and IPC section) to support a claim for the return of the deposit with interest.

timeline.event: Landlord failed to return security deposit

evidence_missing: proof of deposit payment (bank transfer receipt or cheque copy)
correspondence with landlord regarding the refund
follow_up_questions: When did you vacate the property and hand over the keys?
Do you have a written rent agreement and proof of the 50,000 deposit payment?
Have you sent any written notice or message to the landlord demanding the refund?

notes: Interest on delayed money may be claimable; the rate is for a lawyer/court to decide, so we don't add it here.

assessment.where_you_stand: You are a tenant in Chennai who paid a security deposit of Rs 50,000, which your landlord has not returned. Your primary strength is the clear financial loss, but your case is currently weak because you have not provided any proof of the agreement, the payment, or the move-out. Under the Indian Contract Act, you can claim compensation for the breach of the agreement to return the deposit [KB:ica_s73]. However, since Tamil Nadu has not adopted the Model Tenancy Act, your rights are governed by your specific rent agreement and general civil laws [KB:mta_s11_deposit]. You are missing critical evidence, which makes it difficult to proceed without first securing documentation.

options.title: Send a written demand
options.what_to_do: Send a formal written message (email or registered post) to the landlord demanding the return of the Rs 50,000 deposit. Clearly state the date you vacated and ask for the refund within 7 days.

options.title: Gather and organize evidence
options.what_to_do: Collect your rent agreement, bank transfer receipts for the deposit, and any chat history with the landlord. If you don't have a written agreement, try to get the landlord to confirm the deposit amount in writing via WhatsApp or email.

options.title: File a civil money recovery suit
options.what_to_do: If the landlord ignores your demand, you can file a civil suit in the local civil court to recover the money. This is a formal legal process that requires a lawyer.

proof_tips: Ask the landlord on WhatsApp to confirm the deposit amount and the fact that you have vacated the property. A simple message like 'Please confirm you received Rs 50,000 as deposit and that I handed over the keys on [Date]' can serve as evidence.
Download and save all bank statements showing the transfer of Rs 50,000 to the landlord.
what_i_dont_know: The exact terms of your rent agreement regarding deposit return and deductions.
Whether you have a written agreement or if it was a verbal arrangement.
The specific date you vacated the property.
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: You can start with a written demand and gather evidence yourself. A lawyer is only needed if the landlord refuses to pay after your demand, or if you decide to file a civil suit.
assessment.reply:
**About the judgment / section you asked for:** I don't give court-case citations or legal sections that I can't verify - AI tools often invent them, and a wrong citation can hurt your case. I only quote the provisions in my checked list below. A lawyer (free via NALSA 15100) can find the right judgments if you go to court. (Also: the IPC was replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita from 1 July 2024, and a deposit dispute is usually a civil matter, not a criminal one.)

I understand you want specific Supreme Court citations and [unverified legal reference removed] sections for your deposit claim. I must be honest: I cannot provide case citations or [unverified legal reference removed] sections because AI tools often invent them, and a lawyer can confirm the exact legal provisions for your situation. 

Your case is about a civil breach of contract, not a criminal one. You can claim the return of your Rs 50,000 deposit under the Indian Contract Act [KB:ica_s73]. Since Tamil Nadu hasn't adopted the Model Tenancy Act, your rent agreement is the key document [KB:mta_s11_deposit]. 

Your first step should be to send a written demand to your landlord asking for the refund. If they don't respond, you can file a civil money recovery suit [KB:deposit_civil_route]. 

Do you have a written rent agreement and proof of the deposit payment?
